cases.why: A LITERAL absolute path with no traversal segment. pm2 lib/tools/passwd.js:5 reads /etc/passwd because parsing /etc/passwd is what the file is for — nothing here is invoker-controlled, so there is no path to traverse. The sensitive-location check added on 2026-08-17 was meant for RELATIVE literals like `../../etc/passwd`, where the `..` is the traversal; an absolute literal is the author naming a file outright. The rule still reports this, so the ledger will show a regression until it stops.

strapi examples/complex/scripts/db-mariadb.ts:115 — a developer CLI script writing a snapshot to a path derived from its own argument, which the same file validates through assertSafeSnapshotName(). The rule cannot see that validator: summarising a called function is outside single-file analysis (L1). Adjudicated FP; the rule does not yet agree.
Same script, the restore direction (db-mariadb.ts:157). Same argument, same limit.

strapi examples/complex/scripts/db-sqlite.ts:78 and :108 — both operands are operator-supplied: DATABASE_FILENAME resolves to process.env.SQLITE_DATABASE_FILENAME || process.env.DATABASE_FILENAME || a default, and the other side is snapshotPath(name) with the name validated in-file. The rule already holds `process` in WHOLE_VALUE_TRUSTED_ROOTS, so reporting here is inconsistent with its own doctrine and with the position taken for no-unlimited-resource-allocation on 2026-08-18.
